title: ctlv: Add device and operation dispatch
overview: This patch adds drivers/ctlv/core.c, the layer that turns a family descriptor chain into a registered character device and dispatches validated ioctl operations to family callbacks. It builds on the earlier schema, message, blob, builder and event layers and exposes ctlv_create()/ctlv_destroy() plus op-state helpers to family drivers. The Kconfig and Makefile changes enable CONFIG_CTLV and link core.o with the generated root family.

files.purpose: Top-level driver Kconfig; now sources the CTLV menu.

units.title: Hook drivers/ctlv/ into drivers/Kconfig
units.summary: Adds a source line for the ctlv Kconfig between connector and firmware.

units.title: Build drivers/ctlv/ under CONFIG_CTLV
units.summary: Descends into `ctlv/` when `CONFIG_CTLV` is set.

files.purpose: Kbuild rules for the CTLV core module.

units.title: Add core.o and the generated root family object
units.summary: Links `core.o` and the generated `ctlv_gen.o` into `ctlv.o`.
units.details: `ctlv_gen.o` supplies the root family descriptor that `core.c` references as `ctlv_family`.

files.purpose: Core of CTLV: owns device creation and teardown, family chain validation and op table resolution, per-device family priv storage, ioctl op dispatch, the character-device file operations, uevents and the module init. It calls the schema, message, blob and event layers; family drivers call in through `ctlv_create()`, `ctlv_destroy()` and the op provide/state helpers.

units.title: Header, includes
units.summary: License, pr_fmt and the includes core.c needs for cdev, IDA, rwsem and uaccess work.

units.title: Device limit and ABI layout asserts
units.summary: Caps the number of devices and pins the uapi struct sizes and alignment at build time.
units.details: `CTLV_MAX_DEVICES` sizes both the chrdev region and the IDA range. The `static_assert`s guarantee one layout for `ctlv_attr`, `ctlv_op_exec` and `ctlv_event_hdr` on every ABI including compat, which is why `compat_ioctl` can be `compat_ptr_ioctl`.

units.title: Device number, IDA and family priv containers
units.summary: Global device-number base and ID allocator, plus the per-family private-data bookkeeping types.
units.details:
- `ctlv_priv_container` sits immediately before each family's priv, cache-aligned, and links parent and child privs of one device.
- `ctlv_family_priv` records, per chain level, the family, its priv pointer and offset, pending init_info and whether `init` succeeded.

units.title: Family claim registry
units.summary: A global list that binds a family name to its numeric ID for the life of the core module.
units.details: Claims outlive family module unload so an ID can never later name a different family. Protected by `ctlv_family_claims_lock`.

units.title: ctlv_family_claim_add()
units.summary: Records a family name/ID pair, accepting an identical repeat and rejecting a conflicting one.
units.details: Called from `ctlv_create()`. Same ID and same name returns 0; a clash on either alone returns -EEXIST. New claims are kept on `ctlv_family_claims`.

units.title: ctlv_family_claims_free()
units.summary: Frees every claim at module exit.
units.details: Only called from `ctlv_module_exit()`.

units.title: Family validation: error helpers
units.summary: Small helpers that log and return -EINVAL for a malformed family or op descriptor.
units.details: Generated tables should never fail these checks; they exist because an out-of-tree family may come from a different generator.

units.title: ctlv_family_chain_check()
units.summary: Walks from a family up to the core family checking the parent chain, registry ordering and naming rule.
units.details: Each child's name must be its parent's full name plus '-suffix', and parent IDs must be lower than child IDs. The chain must terminate at `&ctlv_family`.

units.title: ctlv_family_descriptor_check()
units.summary: Checks one descriptor in the chain for completeness of its hooks, lifecycle callbacks and extension-point fills.
units.details: Requires a pre/post pair, `priv_size`/`init`/`fini`, no stray claim of the root ID, and that `stub_ops` match the schema's `stub_fill_schemas` one for one.

units.title: ctlv_family_descriptors_check() and ctlv_family_check()
units.summary: Top-level family validation: chain shape first, then each descriptor.
units.details: Called from `ctlv_op_resolution_init()` before any allocation.

units.title: Family priv lookup and free
units.summary: Finds a family's priv slot on a device and releases the priv bookkeeping.
units.details: `ctlv_family_priv_find()` is also used by op resolution and stub lookup. `ctlv_family_privs_free()` is safe to call on partial setup and is reused by the release and error paths.

units.title: ctlv_family_privs_alloc()
units.summary: Lays out one cache-aligned block holding every chain level's priv and links parent/child containers.
units.details:
- First pass sizes each level with overflow-checked arithmetic, ordered oldest ancestor first (index 0 is the core).
- Second pass, after a single `kvzalloc`, aligns the block and wires the `parent`/`child` pointers that `ctlv_priv_parent()`/`ctlv_priv_child()` follow.

units.title: Priv lifecycle: pre_init
units.summary: Threads init_info from the device family up through each ancestor's `pre_init` transform.
units.details: Iterates from the device family towards the core; each level may translate the info for its parent, and the chain must consume it fully by the end.

units.title: Priv lifecycle: pre_fini
units.summary: Runs `pre_fini` on initialized levels, oldest first, with all device locks released.
units.details: The lockdep assertions encode that `pre_fini` may block on consumers and so must not run under registration, transition or events locks.

units.title: Priv lifecycle: init and fini_only
units.summary: Initializes levels core-first and unwinds in reverse; `fini_only` is also the teardown step.
units.details: `initialized` marks which levels have run `init` so a mid-chain failure only finalizes those.

units.title: Priv lifecycle: post_init
units.summary: Runs `post_init` hooks from the device family up to the core after ops are published.
units.details: Failure leaves cleanup to `ctlv_device_fini()` in `ctlv_create()`'s error path.

units.title: ctlv_device_fini()
units.summary: Quiesces a device: drains consumers, stops event contexts and finalizes family privs.
units.details: Order: `pre_fini`, mark `destroying` and stop event contexts under `transition_lock`, wait for contexts, mark the event layer dead, then `fini` each level.

units.title: Op resolution: state and family accounting
units.anchor: /* What one walk of the chain
units.summary: Tracks one walk over the effective schema while binding ops to family callbacks.
units.details: `ctlv_op_resolution_family_bound()` checks that all of a family's bindings were consumed; `ctlv_op_resolution_family_enter()` runs it when the walk moves to the next owner family.

units.title: ctlv_op_resolution_add() - identity and ordering
units.summary: Starts filling one `ctlv_op_entry`: priv, state slot, and op ID ownership and ordering.
units.details: Op IDs encode family and number; the walk from ancestor to descendant must strictly ascend, which also makes IDs unique and lets `ctlv_op_find()` stop early.

units.title: ctlv_op_resolution_add() - type handling
units.summary: Validates and binds actions, queries and events.
units.details:
- Action/query: checks fd access, takes the next binding from the owner family, requires a callback and consistent pre/post hooks, sets `absent` for optional ops.
- Event: no fd access, not optional, assigned a subscription `event_index`.

units.title: ctlv_op_resolution_add() - availability and sizes
units.summary: Assigns dynamic ops a per-device state bit and computes the op's message size limits.
units.details: Dynamic ops index into the `disabled` bitmap; `ctlv_schema_op_sizes()` is evaluated once per device against the target family's filled extension points.

units.title: ctlv_op_resolution_init()
units.summary: Builds the device's sorted op table from the effective schema of the family chain.
units.details: Validates the family, allocates privs, counts ops via the schema cursor, allocates `ctlvdev->ops` and fills it in a second walk, then records dynamic and event counts.

units.title: Priv and device accessors (exported)
units.summary: Public helpers to navigate parent/child family privs and reach the backing device.
units.details: Consumed by family modules through the `CTLV` symbol namespace.

units.title: ctlv_op_find() and ctlv_op_disabled()
units.summary: Looks up an op by ID in the ID-sorted table and tests its dynamic-disable bit.
units.details: The disabled test uses an acquire load, pairing with the fully ordered bit updates in `ctlv_device_op_state_set()`. Dispatch takes no lock for it.

units.title: ctlv_op_publish_all()
units.summary: Drops ops that no family opted into and freezes the table.
units.details: Compacts the array in place under `transition_lock` and sets `published`, after which lookups see a stable table.

units.title: ctlv_device_op_provide()
units.summary: Lets a family opt an optional op in before publication.
units.details: Only valid before publish and not during destroy; clears `absent` on the entry. Backs the `CTLV_OP_PROVIDE()` macro.

units.title: ctlv_device_op_state_set()
units.summary: Enables or disables a dynamic op and announces the change to event subscribers.
units.details: Serialized by `transition_lock`; a no-op change returns early, and after publication it bumps `state_generation` and calls `ctlv_event_op_changed()` while still holding the lock so queues see ordered records. Backs `CTLV_OP_ENABLE()`/`CTLV_OP_DISABLE()`.

units.title: Op execution: mode check and reply sizing
units.summary: Checks the open file mode against the op's fd access and gives the minimum reply size for an op.
units.details: Events cannot be executed. READ_WRITE ops need both modes on the descriptor.

units.title: Request framing and validation
units.summary: Checks the root attribute frame and validates the request against the op's request schema.
units.details: `ctlv_request_frame()` sets `CTLV_VALIDATION_REASON_MALFORMED_MESSAGE` on a bad frame; `ctlv_request_validate()` then runs `ctlv_schema_validate()` and leaves an index in `ctx->request` that is freed by `ctlv_op_exec()`.

units.title: ctlv_reply_capacity()
units.summary: Chooses the reply buffer size: schema maximum for actions, caller's length for queries.
units.details: Returns 0 when the op has no reply schema.

units.title: Reply completion checks
units.summary: Verifies after the callback that the built reply is complete and schema-valid.
units.details: Queries mid-stream (cursor outstanding) skip full validation; a successful query callback must have ended exactly one fragment.

units.title: ctlv_op_call()
units.summary: Invokes the bound action or query callback with request and reply cursors and finalizes blob handling.
units.details: Wraps the call in `ctlv_blob_context_init()`/`ctlv_blob_context_finish()` and then runs `ctlv_reply_finish()` on success.

units.title: ctlv_op_dispatch()
units.summary: Applies the family-level and op-level pre/post hooks around the availability check and the call.
units.details: Core-family ops use the core hooks and priv; others use the device family's. Hook order is family pre, op pre, call (or -EOPNOTSUPP if disabled), op post, family post.

units.title: ctlv_error_info()
units.summary: Replaces the reply with an error-info message describing a validation or callback failure, if it fits.
units.details: Builds a separate buffer using `ctlv_error_info_schema`; stale-generation errors carry generations, others carry offsets and a missing attr ID. The errno stays authoritative.

units.title: ctlv_op_exec() - lookup and argument checks
units.summary: Resolves the op and checks mode, resume fields and reply length before touching any buffers.
units.details: Only queries accept `generation`/`cursor`; a too-small reply buffer is rejected up front so nothing is mutated.

units.title: ctlv_op_exec() - snapshot, dispatch, reply
units.summary: Copies and validates the request, allocates the reply, dispatches and hands the reply to the caller.
units.details: The request is snapshotted so hooks never read userspace. On success `exec->generation` and `exec->cursor` are updated and `*reply` takes ownership of the buffer; on failure error info may replace it.

units.title: ctlv_stub_ops_find()
units.anchor: /* What one family of this device's chain
units.summary: Finds the family in this device's chain that filled a given extension point.
units.details: Searches from the device family towards the core and returns that family's stub ops and priv.

units.title: ctlv_stub_fill()
units.summary: Delegates an extension-point output nest to the family that filled it.
units.details: Called from generated helpers. It rebinds the request cursor to the fill schema's members when a request is present, then invokes the stub's `fill` callback.

units.title: Core family callbacks
units.summary: No-op hooks and lifecycle callbacks the core supplies for the generated root family descriptor.
units.details: `ctlv_init()` only asserts the core has no init_info and no parent priv.

units.title: ctlv_file_ioctl()
units.summary: Handles `CTLV_IOC_OP_EXEC`: copies the exec struct, runs the op under the registration read lock and copies results out.
units.details: Takes `registration_lock` for read, so `ctlv_destroy()` waits for admitted callbacks. Reply copy-out happens after the lock is dropped; only `generation` and `cursor` are written back into the user struct.

units.title: ctlv_file_read() and ctlv_file_poll()
units.summary: Event delivery entry points that forward to the event layer.
units.details: Read returns one record per call; both delegate to `ctlv_event_file_read()`/`ctlv_event_file_poll()` in event.c.

units.title: File open admission helpers
units.summary: Predicate that the device is registered and has a family.
units.details: Must be called with the registration read lock held.

units.title: ctlv_file_open()
units.summary: Admits an open: pins the device, allocates a per-file context and initializes its event queue.
units.details: Takes a device reference first so a failed create cannot free storage under a waiting open. The reference is kept by the file and released in `ctlv_file_release()`.

units.title: ctlv_file_release()
units.summary: Tears down the per-file event state and drops the device reference.
units.details: Counterpart of `ctlv_file_open()`.

units.title: File operations table
units.summary: Wires the char-device entry points to the functions above.
units.details: `owner` is the core module, not the family's, so an open file does not hold a family module.

units.title: Uevent family identity
units.summary: Emits `CTLV_FAMILY` and a `CTLV_COMPATIBLE_<n>` list of the chain's names, plus a count.
units.details: Gives udev rules the family chain before the node can be opened.

units.title: ctlv_device_uevent_check()
units.summary: Dry-runs the uevent environment at create time to catch names too long for a uevent.
units.details: Run before a minor is allocated; returns -E2BIG with a diagnostic if limits are exceeded.

units.title: ctlv_device_uevent() and release
units.summary: Class uevent callback and the device release callback.
units.details: Uevent reads `family` with `READ_ONCE` without the registration lock. Release frees the IDA slot, disabled bitmap, privs, ops and the device itself.

units.title: Device class
units.summary: Class under which every CTLV device node appears.
units.details: Registered in `ctlv_module_init()`.

units.title: ctlv_device_add() and ctlv_device_del()
units.summary: Thin wrappers around `cdev_device_add()` and `cdev_device_del()`.
units.details: Add requires the registration write lock to be held.

units.title: ctlv_create() - allocation and resolution
units.summary: Allocates the device and resolves ops, event sizes, the uevent check and the disabled bitmap.
units.details: Exported entry point for family drivers. Failures here use the plain `err_free` path since `device_initialize()` has not run.

units.title: ctlv_create() - registration and unwind
units.summary: Allocates a minor, initializes the device, runs the family lifecycle and publishes the device.
units.details:
- After `device_initialize()`, errors use `put_device()` (release callback frees storage).
- Order: claim add, pre_init, init, publish ops, start event contexts, post_init, then `cdev_device_add()` under the write lock and set `registered`.
- `err_fini` runs `ctlv_device_fini()` first.

units.title: ctlv_destroy()
units.summary: Unregisters the device, waits out admitted callbacks, finalizes the family and drops the device.
units.details: Removes the node, clears `registered` under the write lock (draining in-flight ioctls), runs `ctlv_device_fini()`, then detaches family pointers so no callback can reach family-owned state.

units.title: Module init and exit
units.summary: Reserves the char-device region and registers the class; exit reverses it and frees claims and the IDA.
units.details: Registered at `subsys_initcall` so family drivers can create devices at their init.

files.purpose: Private definition of `struct ctlv_device`, shared among core.c and event.c.

units.title: struct ctlv_device additions
units.summary: Adds the cdev, registration lock, family priv array and op availability state to the device.
units.details:
- `registration_lock` (rwsem) guards `registered` and `family`; ioctls read-lock it, create/destroy write-lock it.
- `transition_lock` serializes op publication and state writers; dispatch never takes it.
- `disabled` is the bitmap of dynamic ops.

files.purpose: Public API for CTLV users; this patch adds device lifecycle and priv navigation.

units.title: Priv navigation and device create/destroy API
units.summary: Declares kernel-doc for priv parent/child, backing device, `ctlv_create()` and `ctlv_destroy()`.

units.title: ctlv_stub_fill() declaration
units.summary: Declares the extension-point delegation helper used by generated code.

files.purpose: Interface between the core and family modules.

units.title: Op provide and state-set declarations
units.summary: Exports the family-facing functions for optional-op opt-in and dynamic enable/disable.

units.title: CTLV_OP_PROVIDE/ENABLE/DISABLE macros
units.summary: Generates per-op inline wrappers `<name>_provide/_enable/_disable` around the two functions.
units.details: Generated headers instantiate these with each op's ID.
